comments.content: This `reinterpret_cast` on a `shared_ptr` is undefined behavior. `std::shared_ptr<std::list<std::shared_ptr<ModelLibraryLocal>>>` and `std::shared_ptr<std::list<std::shared_ptr<ModelLibrary>>>` are unrelated types; reinterpreting the shared_ptr object itself is not valid. Since `ModelLibraryLocal` derives from `ModelLibrary`, you can safely construct a new shared_ptr with a converting constructor: `return std::shared_ptr<std::list<std::shared_ptr<ModelLibrary>>>(_libraryList);` (or build a new list by copying elements).
`cleanup()` returns immediately after calling `ModelManagerLocal::cleanup()`, so the external manager cleanup below is dead code. Remove the `return` or restructure so both cleanups run.

`_useExternal` is a static member but is written from `OnChange` without holding `_mutex`, while other code paths (e.g. `getLibraries`, `getModel`) read it concurrently. This is a data race. Guard the write with `QMutexLocker locker(&_mutex);` (and consider making the reads consistent as well).

`getModel` caches `nullptr` for `ModelNotFound`/`ConnectionError`. Caching a negative result for a connection error means a transient network failure will be remembered until the cache entry is evicted, so subsequent lookups will keep returning null even after connectivity is restored. Consider only caching successful lookups, or at least not caching on `ConnectionError`.

`_cache` is a static member shared across instances, but `getModel` accesses it without holding `_mutex` (only `initCache` locks). Concurrent access from multiple threads is a data race. Lock `_mutex` around cache reads/writes, or use a thread-safe cache.
Missing newline at end of file.
The `catch` blocks swallow exceptions silently. At minimum log the error (e.g. `Base::Console().Warning(...)`) so failures in the external manager are diagnosable.

`isLocalLibrary` returns `false` only when the external manager returns a non-null library. If the external lookup throws `ConnectionError` (not caught here), the exception propagates. Also, if `_useExternal` is true but the library is not found externally, it falls through to `return true`, which is correct, but the `LibraryNotFound` catch is empty and hides the reason. Consider logging.

`migrateToExternal` calls `_externalManager->createLibrary(...)` and then iterates local models. If `createLibrary` throws (e.g. `ConnectionError`), the migration aborts mid-way with no rollback. Consider documenting/handling partial migration.

`validateMigration` calls `model->validate(externalModel)` without checking that `externalModel` is non-null. `ModelManagerExternal::getModel` can return `nullptr` (e.g. on cache miss + `ModelNotFound`), which would likely crash or assert inside `validate`. Add a null check.

In `getModelTree`, `ModelManager::getManager().getModel(getName(), uuid)` may return `nullptr` (external manager can return null on cache miss/error), and the code immediately dereferences `model->getType()`. Add a null check before use.

`ModelLibrary(const Library& other)` is declared but the base `Library` copy constructor is user-defined; ensure `ModelLibrary`'s copy constructor is not implicitly deleted by the `= delete` on `ModelLibrary(const ModelLibrary&)`. Since `ModelLibrary(const Library&)` is a converting constructor (not a copy ctor), this is fine, but note that `ModelLibraryLocal(const Library&)` similarly relies on `ModelLibrary(const Library&)`.

`initCache` is called from the constructor and locks `_mutex`, but `_cache` is a static member initialized before any instance exists. `_cache.capacity(cacheSize)` and `_cache.monitor()` mutate shared state; if multiple `ModelManagerExternal` instances are constructed (or `initCache` is called concurrently), this is fine under the lock, but note that `_cache` is shared across all instances, so per-instance cache size configuration is global. This may be intentional but worth documenting.
